title: Policy DSL + Safety Curator for throughput-targeted scaling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
We need a concise, expressive policy DSL and a runtime 'safety curator' that together allow SREs and platform engineers to declare throughput guarantees (requests/sec or tokens/sec), choose scaling algorithms (rule-based stepper, PID-like integrator, and quantile headroom allocator), and attach safety limits (max step, slope limit, reserve headroom, cooldown windows). The goal is to move from ad-hoc autoscaling knobs to repeatable, verifiable policy artifacts that can be validated in staging and applied to Dedicated fleets without manual intervention.

Scope: DSL syntax, compiler to runtime rule sets, safety curator that enforces per-tenant/global limits, simulation harness for backtesting policies against production traces, and telemetry hooks for policy-level observability. Not in scope: autoscaler orchestration plumbing (already in other tickets), or UI surface for composing policies (separate design task).
design_notes: Policy primitive types: target_metric (throughput_rps | throughput_tps | p95_latency_ms | concurrency), smoothing_window (seconds), target_quantile (for latency-driven policies), and min_headroom_pct

Three algorithm modes: stepper (saturated step-ups with backoff), integrator (PI-like with derivative dampening), predictive-credit (uses demand forecast to pre-assign headroom credits), and hybrid composition via 'compose' operator
Safety curator functions: clamp(max_instances, global_pool_quota), slope_limit(max_instances_per_minute), reserve_credit(account_id, tokens), emergency_fallback(model_variant)
Compiler will emit: target_metric expression, evaluation frequency, action intent (scale-to, scale-by, credit-assign), and safety annotations for the orchestrator to honor
decisions: Adopt a declarative DSL that compiles to an intermediate runtime policy object rather than shipping an interpreter in each agent — simplifies validation & testing.

Default target metric for Dedicated tiers will be throughput_rps with optional token-based variants; latency-driven policies allowed but require explicit customer opt-in because of risk to throughput guarantees.
Safety-first: all scale intents must be checked by Safety Curator which can reject, re-write (apply clamps), or downgrade requests to a slower algorithm (eg. from stepper -> integrator).
Use existing tracing + metrics pipeline for policy-level telemetry (no separate agent) — will add dedicated tags: policy.key, intent.type, safety.action
tradeoffs: Declarative DSL reduces expressiveness vs. Turing-complete policy scripts, but improves auditability and allows static verification.
Compiling centrally increases latency between policy change and fleet rollout but enables thorough policy validation and simulation before application.
Conservative default safety limits reduce risk of overshoot but may underutilize hardware for bursty tenants; we provide explicit escape hatches for verified customers.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with SRE, runtime, and product. Agreed on primary metrics and safety primitives.
2026-03-04: Prototype DSL grammar drafted (see Confluence). Basic 'scale_by' and 'scale_to' primitives present.
2026-03-06: Implemented initial compiler emitting runtime policy JSON and basic simulator harness that replays recent production traces.
2026-03-09: First integration test: policy compiler + safety curator applied to a small staging fleet; safety curator clamped a step-up for tenant T-224 as expected.
2026-03-10: Security review triage completed — no immediate crypto or secret handling concerns identified.
acceptance_criteria: DSL grammar stable for v1 and committed to repo with unit tests
Compiler emits runtime policy objects that pass static schema validation
Safety Curator enforces: max_instances, slope_limit, and reserve_credit in staging run without human intervention
Simulator shows <2% false-positive safety clamps on 72h production trace replay for 3 representative tenants
End-to-end test: deploy policy to staging fleet, observe intent -> orchestrator -> scaling action -> metrics within 10 minutes with safety intervention logged
testing_plan: Unit tests for grammar and compiler transformation
Simulator-based policy backtests on multiple tenant traces including bursty, seasonal, and long-tail patterns
Chaos test: inject spurious high throughput signals to ensure safety clamps prevent runaway scaling
Staging rollout: staged canary across 3 dedicated racks with feature-flag toggles
next_steps: Finalize DSL edgecases (composing policies, override semantics) by 2026-03-12
Extend simulator to include KV-cache hit-rate correlation analysis (2026-03-15)
Prepare customer-facing policy examples and migration guide for Dedicated tenants (by 2026-03-18)
